messages.text: Warner slams 'pathetic' Test crowds in South Africa

metadata.summary: Former batter David Warner has hit out at the "pathetic" attendances in the ongoing Test series between South Africa and Australia.
metadata.content: David Warner slams 'pathetic' crowds for South Africa vs Australia Test matches | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content David Warner slams 'pathetic' crowds for South Africa vs Australia Test matches The first Test between South Africa and Australia in Durban was less than a fifth full over the course of the five days; the Kwa-Zulu Natal Cricket Union (KZNCU) have said they will launch a "thorough internal review" into the poorly-attended match at Kingsmead Tuesday 20 October 2026 12:30, UK Image: A cricket supporter sits alone in the stands during the first Test between South Africa and Australia in Durban Former batter David Warner has hit out at the "pathetic" attendances in the ongoing Test series between South Africa and Australia. South Africa lost the first Test match by 214 runs in Durban , with large sections of the Kingsmead ground empty, and the crowds haven't really picked up through the first two rain-affected days of the second Test in Gqeberha. "We keep hearing how important Test cricket is, but where are the fans in South Africa?" former opener Warner said in a social media post on Tuesday. messages.text: Boulter puts rain delays behind her to progress at Japan Open

metadata.summary: A day after heavy rainfall caused play to be suspended, Britain's Katie Boulter returned to clinch a 6-3 6-1 victory at the Japan Open over wildcard Himeno Sakatsume.
metadata.content: Japan Open: Katie Boulter puts rain delays behind her as Brit progresses to second round in Osaka | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Japan Open: Katie Boulter puts rain delays behind her as Brit progresses to second round in Osaka Britain's Katie Boulter books place in second round of Japan Open, after defeating home wildcard Himeno Sakatsume; Play had been suspended the day before due to heavy rainfall in Osaka; Watch the Japan Open all this week, live on Sky Sports Tennis Tuesday 20 October 2026 08:41, UK Image: Britain's Katie Boulter progressed to the second round of the Japan Open after victory over Himeno Sakatsume A day after heavy rainfall caused play to be suspended, Britain's Katie Boulter returned to clinch a 6-3 6-1 victory at the Japan Open over wildcard Himeno Sakatsume. The world No 58 concluded a dominant victory in one hour and 32 minutes in Osaka, and she will next face Swiss player Viktorija Golubic for a place in the quarter-finals. The victory gives Boulter a 20-20 record across her last 40 matches, and a confidence boost following a period in which she has only played three matches since September 30, owing to early exits at the China Open (second round) and Wuhan Open (first round). messages.text: England unchanged for World Cup clash vs France with Lewis absent again

metadata.summary: England head coach Brian McDermott has stuck with the same 19-man squad that were thrashed 30-12 by Tonga in the tournament opener for Saturday's Rugby League World Cup clash against France.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: Mikey Lewis absent again as England unchanged for clash vs France despite opening defeat | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby League World Cup: Mikey Lewis absent again as England unchanged for clash vs France despite opening defeat England take on France in Perth on Saturday (7.35am kick-off BST) for second Rugby League World Cup fixture, having been thrashed by Tonga in opener; England play Papua New Guinea in Wollongong on October 30; England Women began their campaign with big win vs Wales in Perth Tuesday 20 October 2026 07:48, UK Image: Mikey Lewis will not feature for England again as England opt for unchanged squad England head coach Brian McDermott has stuck with the same 19-man squad that were thrashed 30-12 by Tonga in the tournament opener for Saturday's Rugby League World Cup clash against France. AJ Brimson retains the job at full-back with Jack Welsby again named as an interchange, while Luke Thompson starts at prop in the absence of Morgan Knowles, who suffered an injury in the lead-up to the opening game against Tonga. Veteran centre Kallum Watkins is listed among the reserves as he chases a cap at his fourth World Cup, while there also remains no place in the squad for Mikey Lewis. As per World Cup rules, each side is able to name a six-player bench in each game, but only four of the six players named can be brought on. messages.text: Reese scores 30 points as Atlanta win at Golden State to level WNBA Finals

metadata.summary: Angel Reese delivered 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals after she struggled down the stretch in the series opener, as the Atlanta Dream stymied the Golden State Valkyries at both ends in the second half to win 79-65 and level the best-of-seven series at 1-1.
metadata.content: WNBA Finals: Angel Reese scores 30 points, 16 rebounds as Atlanta Dream win at Golden State Valkyries to level best-of-seven series 1-1 | NBA News | Sky Sports Skip to main content WNBA Finals: Angel Reese scores 30 points, 16 rebounds as Atlanta Dream win at Golden State Valkyries to level best-of-seven series 1-1 Atlanta Dream level WNBA Finals at 1-1 in best-of-seven series as they secure 79-65 away win at Golden State Valkyries; Angel Reese proves star with 30 points and 16 rebounds - third player ever to register such stats in a Finals game; watch WNBA Finals live on Sky Sports Tuesday 20 October 2026 07:10, UK Image: Angel Reese proved the standout as the Atlanta Dream levelled the WNBA Finals 1-1 vs Golden State Valkyries Angel Reese delivered 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals after she struggled down the stretch in the series opener, as the Atlanta Dream stymied the Golden State Valkyries at both ends in the second half to win 79-65 and level the best-of-seven series at 1-1. In front of the Valkyries' raucous home crowd, the Atlanta star had no choice but to raise her voice - and Reese knew she had to raise her game, too. "For me, I think I let my team down last game not really contributing as much as I could in the second half," Reese said. "Not even just about scoring, my screen quality, me hustling and running to get rebounds, just doing the things that they know me to do.
